Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space.

- For $0<p<\infty$, define an equivalence relation on $\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ by
  $$f\sim g\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f-g\in\mathcal N(\mu),$$
  and write $L^p(\mu)$ for the set of classes $[f]$.
- For $p=\infty$, define the same relation on $L^\infty(\mu)$ and again write
  $L^\infty(\mu)$ for the set of classes.

Thus an element of $L^p(\mu)$ is an almost-everywhere equivalence class of
measurable representatives.

When $1\le p\le\infty$, the displayed set quotient agrees with the usual
quotient-vector-space construction of
[[def-quotient-vector-space-and-canonical-projection]].

For $0<p<1$, the same class notation is used; under its stated choice hypothesis, the later item
[[thm-the-l-p-distance-for-zero-less-p-less-one-is-a-complete-translation-invariant-metric]]
supplies the metric structure rather than a normed-space structure.

Adopt as a physical assumption of the pair, additional to P1, P2 and P4 and
valid only for the declared finite-level model of this clause, the following
static electric-dipole coupling. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the
Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(i) Declared charged pair and relative coordinate.** Take the declared
two-body Coulomb model of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] clause (d): two
distinguishable spinless particles with mass parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ and
opposite charges $-q$ and $+q$, $q>0$ (coulombs), with the relative coordinate
$r=x_{1}-x_{2}$ and the centre-of-mass/relative unitary
$U_{\Phi}$. Work in the relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb
R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of that reading, with Coulomb mass parameter $m=\mu:=m_{1}m_{2}/(m_{1}+m_{2})$, and with units as in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(ii) Dipole operator.** Let $Q_{j}$, $j=1,2,3$, be the coordinate
multiplication operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with maximal
domains $D(Q_{j})=\{\psi:\xi_{j}\psi\in L^{2}\}$ of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-atomic-dipole-matrix-element-domain]] clause (a); they are
self-adjoint and proper densely defined. The model's **dipole operator** is
the triple
$$D_{j}:=-q\,Q_{j}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
because the dipole of charges $-q$ at $x_{1}$ and $+q$ at $x_{2}$ is
$-qx_{1}+qx_{2}=-qr$: it points from the negative to the positive charge,
opposite to the declared relative coordinate $r=x_{1}-x_{2}$. Each $D_{j}$ is
self-adjoint on $D(Q_{j})$ and has unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$. This is the dipole of
the declared pair in its relative-coordinate reading; no multipole expansion,
no field equation and no coupling to the centre-of-mass motion is assumed.

**(iii) Finite-level truncation.** Fix, as part of the model specification, a
**declared finite-dimensional subspace** $W\subseteq D(H_\kappa)\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap
D(Q_{3})$ of the relative-coordinate space with $D(H_\kappa)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and $\dim W=d<\infty$, together
with an orthonormal basis of $W$. The model declares the **compressed dipole
matrix** on $W$,
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W},$$
where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$ and the restriction to
$W$ is read in the declared orthonormal basis; $D^{W}_{j}$ is the finite
Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix of the dipole component, with unit
$\mathrm{C\,m}$, and it is bounded with norm at most $\sup_{\psi\in
W,\|\psi\|=1}\|D_{j}\psi\|$. The truncation and the basis are model
assumptions: they are not derived from the Coulomb model, and they replace
the unbounded operator $D_{j}$ by its compression throughout this pair.

**(iv) Static uniform field and interaction operator.** The external datum is
a **uniform static electric field value** $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\in\mathbb
R^{3}$, read in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$; it is prescribed, and no Maxwell
equation, source model, propagation or back-reaction is assumed. The
**finite-level static Stark model** is the finite-dimensional operator on $W$
$$H_{S}(\mathbf E_{\rm ext}):=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W} -\sum_{j=1}^{3}E_{{\rm ext},j}\,D^{W}_{j},$$
where the energy-domain condition of (iii) makes the compression defined,
and $H_{\kappa}=C_{\mu}$ is the one-centre Coulomb energy operator with
mass parameter $m=\mu$ of the declared model, read on the relative-coordinate
factor through the angular/radial
identification used by the pair. The interaction term has unit
$\mathrm{C\,m\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm J$ and is bounded Hermitian on $W$, so
$H_{S}(\mathbf E_{\rm ext})$ is a bounded Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix and
the Kato-Rellich and perturbation statements of the pair apply to it with a
bounded perturbation; this identification of the matrix with the model's
energy on the truncated subspace is a model assumption.

**(v) Scope and explicit exclusion.** Clauses (i)-(iv) are adopted model
assumptions. They assert nothing about a laboratory atom, field or apparatus;
no measured Stark shift is claimed; no transition, absorption or emission
rate is defined; and no time dependence of the field is assumed. In
particular the postulate deliberately does **not** treat the uncompressed
linear potential $-\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf D$ as a bounded
perturbation of $H_{\kappa}$: the uncompressed term is an unbounded
multiplication operator, and the energy form of $H_{\kappa}$ plus that term
has no lower bound for a nonzero field, so the uncompressed static-field model
is outside the scope of every statement of this pair. Only the compressed
finite-level operator of clause (iv) is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $M$ be a closed linear subspace of a real or complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). By the orthogonal-decomposition theorem ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]) every $x\in H$ has a unique representation

$$x=P_Mx+(x-P_Mx),\qquad P_Mx\in M,\quad x-P_Mx\in M^\perp ,$$

and the **Hilbert orthogonal projection onto $M$** is the map

$$P_M:H\longrightarrow M\subseteq H,\qquad x\longmapsto P_Mx ,$$

assigning to $x$ its unique $M$-component. Its defining properties are therefore

$$P_Mx\in M,\qquad x-P_Mx\in M^\perp\qquad(x\in H),$$

which characterise $P_M$ uniquely: a map with these defining properties must agree with the $M$-component of the unique decomposition of each $x$.

**Agreement with the finite-dimensional projection.** If $V$ is a finite-dimensional inner-product space and $W\subseteq V$ a subspace, then [[thm-finite-dimensional-orthogonal-decomposition]] writes $V=W\oplus W^\perp$ and [[def-orthogonal-projection]] defines $P_Wv$ as the unique $W$-component of $v$; the defining properties displayed above are the same, so they define the same map on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.

**Range and kernel.** $P_Mx\in M$ for every $x$, and $P_Mm=m$ for $m\in M$ because $m=m+0$ with $0\in M^\perp$; conversely $P_Mx=0$ says exactly that $x=x-0\in M^\perp$. Hence the range of $P_M$ is $M$ and its kernel is $M^\perp$, and $P_M$ is the identity on $M$ and zero on $M^\perp$.

Let $H$ be a real or complex inner-product space ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), with inner
product linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, and
with the induced length $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$. The definitions below
do not require completeness. When the term *Hilbert basis* is used, $H$ is
additionally assumed complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]).

**Orthonormal indexed family.** Let $I$ be any set. An indexed family
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of vectors of $H$ is **orthonormal** when

$$\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}:=\begin{cases}1,&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j,\end{cases} \qquad\text{for all } i,j\in I .$$Because $1\ne 0$ in the scalar field, the family contains no zero vector: $\|e_i\|^2=\langle e_i,e_i\rangle=1$, so $\|e_i\|=1$ for every $i$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); and the index map is injective, since $e_i=e_j$ with $i\ne j$ would give $0=\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=1$. Thus an orthonormal family is the same thing as an orthonormal set together with a labelling of it, and in the sequel no choice is hidden in passing between the two descriptions. **Orthonormal set.** A subset $S\subseteq H$ is **orthonormal** when every $s\in S$ has $\|s\|=1$ and $\langle s,t\rangle=0$ for all distinct $s,t\in S$. For such an $S$ the family $(e_s)_{s\in S}$ with $e_s:=s$ is orthonormal in the indexed sense, and the image of an orthonormal indexed family is an orthonormal set. Orthogonal means $\langle s,t\rangle=0$ ([[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]). **Independence and unique coefficients.** Let $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be orthonormal, let $F\subseteq I$ be finite, and let scalars $c_i$ satisfy $\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i=0$. For each fixed $j\in F$, linearity in the first argument gives$$0=\Bigl\langle \sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i,\;e_j\Bigr\rangle=\sum_{i\in F}c_i\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=c_j ,$$

so every finite subfamily of an orthonormal family is linearly independent. In
particular the coefficients in a finite expansion are unique: if
$\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i=\sum_{i\in F}d_ie_i$, then applying the computation to
$c-d$ gives $c_i=d_i$ for every $i\in F$.

**Closed linear span and completeness.** The **span** of an indexed family is
the set of all finite linear combinations $\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i$ with $F\subseteq I$
finite and scalars $c_i$; it is the smallest linear subspace of $H$ containing
every $e_i$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). Its closure in the induced norm is the
**closed linear span** of the family, the smallest closed linear subspace of $H$
containing every $e_i$. The family is **complete**, or is a **complete
orthonormal system**, when its closed linear span is all of $H$. A
**Hilbert basis**, or **orthonormal basis**, of $H$ is a complete orthonormal
family in $H$.

**The empty family.** The span of the empty family is $\{0\}$, which is already
closed, so the empty family is complete exactly when $H=\{0\}$. Thus the zero
Hilbert space always has a Hilbert basis, namely the empty one.

**Not a Hamel basis, and no order is assumed.** A Hilbert basis is a basis only
in the sense of closed linear span: for an infinite-dimensional $H$ the vectors
of $H$ are in general **not** finite linear combinations of a Hilbert basis, and
the expansion of an arbitrary vector is a norm limit of finite partial sums, not
a finite sum. No enumeration, ordering or countability of the index set is part
of the definition; the partial sums are indexed by the finite subsets of $I$,
ordered by inclusion, and that is the convention used on this page.

**Coefficient notation.** For orthonormal $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ and $x\in H$ the
scalars $\langle x,e_i\rangle$ are the **coefficients** of $x$ with respect to
the family. They are well defined for every $x$, without any assumption that
the family is complete.

[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-atomic-dipole-matrix-element-domain]] clause (a); they are
self-adjoint and proper densely defined. The model's **dipole operator** is
the triple
$$D_{j}:=-q\,Q_{j}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
because the dipole of charges $-q$ at $x_{1}$ and $+q$ at $x_{2}$ is
$-qx_{1}+qx_{2}=-qr$: it points from the negative to the positive charge,
opposite to the declared relative coordinate $r=x_{1}-x_{2}$. Each $D_{j}$ is
self-adjoint on $D(Q_{j})$ and has unit $\mathrm{C\,m}$. This is the dipole of
the declared pair in its relative-coordinate reading; no multipole expansion,
no field equation and no coupling to the centre-of-mass motion is assumed.

**(iii) Finite-level truncation.** Fix, as part of the model specification, a
**declared finite-dimensional subspace** $W\subseteq D(H_\kappa)\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap
D(Q_{3})$ of the relative-coordinate space with $D(H_\kappa)=H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ and $\dim W=d<\infty$, together
with an orthonormal basis of $W$. The model declares the **compressed dipole
matrix** on $W$,
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W},$$
where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$ and the restriction to
$W$ is read in the declared orthonormal basis; $D^{W}_{j}$ is the finite
Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix of the dipole component, with unit
$\mathrm{C\,m}$, and it is bounded with norm at most $\sup_{\psi\in
W,\|\psi\|=1}\|D_{j}\psi\|$. The truncation and the basis are model
assumptions: they are not derived from the Coulomb model, and they replace
the unbounded operator $D_{j}$ by its compression throughout this pair.

**(iv) Static uniform field and interaction operator.** The external datum is
a **uniform static electric field value** $\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\in\mathbb
R^{3}$, read in $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$; it is prescribed, and no Maxwell
equation, source model, propagation or back-reaction is assumed. The
**finite-level static Stark model** is the finite-dimensional operator on $W$
$$H_{S}(\mathbf E_{\rm ext}):=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W} -\sum_{j=1}^{3}E_{{\rm ext},j}\,D^{W}_{j},$$
where the energy-domain condition of (iii) makes the compression defined,
and $H_{\kappa}=C_{\mu}$ is the one-centre Coulomb energy operator with
mass parameter $m=\mu$ of the declared model, read on the relative-coordinate
factor through the angular/radial
identification used by the pair. The interaction term has unit
$\mathrm{C\,m\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm J$ and is bounded Hermitian on $W$, so
$H_{S}(\mathbf E_{\rm ext})$ is a bounded Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix and
the Kato-Rellich and perturbation statements of the pair apply to it with a
bounded perturbation; this identification of the matrix with the model's
energy on the truncated subspace is a model assumption.

**(v) Scope and explicit exclusion.** Clauses (i)-(iv) are adopted model
assumptions. They assert nothing about a laboratory atom, field or apparatus;
no measured Stark shift is claimed; no transition, absorption or emission
rate is defined; and no time dependence of the field is assumed. In
particular the postulate deliberately does **not** treat the uncompressed
linear potential $-\mathbf E_{\rm ext}\cdot\mathbf D$ as a bounded
perturbation of $H_{\kappa}$: the uncompressed term is an unbounded
multiplication operator, and the energy form of $H_{\kappa}$ plus that term
has no lower bound for a nonzero field, so the uncompressed static-field model
is outside the scope of every statement of this pair. Only the compressed
finite-level operator of clause (iv) is used.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the static finite-level dipole postulate
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]], in the state
and outcome readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], in the radiation
sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and in the units and dimensions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited Fock space
mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Finite-level matter factor.** Take the declared charged pair, the
relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the coordinate
multipliers $Q_{j}$ and the dipole operator components $D_{j}=-q\,Q_{j}$ of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses
(i)-(ii), with the Coulomb energy operator $H_{\kappa}$ of clause (iv) of that
postulate. Fix, as model data, a declared finite-dimensional subspace
$$W\subseteq D(H_{\kappa})\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap D(Q_{3}),\qquad \dim W=d<\infty,$$
with a declared orthonormal basis $(w_{1},\dots,w_{d})$ of $W$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and read $W$ as $\mathbb C^{d}$ in that basis. The model's **compressed matter
energy** is the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix
$$H_{a}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W},$$
read in joules, where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); the model's **compressed dipole
matrices** are the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
read in $\mathrm{C\,m}$; and the model's **levels** are the pairs $(E,v)$ with
$E\in\mathbb R$ (joules) an eigenvalue of $H_{a}$ and $v\in\mathbb C^{d}$ a
nonzero eigenvector for $E$. A **declared level pair** is an ordered pair
$(a,b)$ of orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{a},v_{b}$ of $H_{a}$; its **transition
energy** is $E_{a}-E_{b}$. The subspace, its basis and its dimension are model
data: they are not derived from the Coulomb model and they replace the
unbounded operators $H_{\kappa},D_{j}$ by their compressions throughout this
pair.

**(c) Radiation factor and cutoff dipole data.** Take the transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h$, the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$, the
vacuum $\Omega$, the sector projections $\Pi_{n}$ and the free-field energy
observable $H_{f}=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]]
clauses (b),(d), with the domains and self-adjointness of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], read in
joules. Fix, as further model data, a **cutoff** $\Lambda>0$ (joules), an
integer $J\ge1$ and vectors $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
and a real **coupling number** $\eta_{0}$ declared so that the interaction term
of clause (d) is read in joules. The cutoff and the mode vectors are model
data; no laboratory mode content, no Maxwell field, no mode density and no
value of $\eta_{0}$ is asserted.

**(d) The coupled model.** Write $\phi(g):=A_{-}(g)+A_{+}(g)$ for the maximal
creation-annihilation sum of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] on
$F(\mathfrak h)$. The **declared finite-level cutoff dipole model** is the pair
of the Hilbert space $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and the operator
$$H_{\mathrm{LM}}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}+\eta_{0}\sum_{j=1}^{J}D^{W}_{j}\otimes\phi(g_{j}), \qquad D(H_{\mathrm{LM}}):=\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f}).$$
By [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] clause (c),
read with the Hermitian matrices $H_{a}$, $D^{W}_{1},\dots,D^{W}_{J}$ and the
coupling $\eta_{0}$ (its $d$ is the present $d$), the operator
$H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ is self-adjoint on the displayed domain and bounded below
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). The model declares $H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ its
**energy observable**, in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], with energies,
mode energies and the coupling read in joules.

**(e) The model's evolution and states.** The model's evolution is the
autonomous unitary family $U(t):=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}$, $t\in\mathbb R$,
in the reading of clause (iv) of P4 and of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; a preparation $\rho$ of
the model is a state of $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], with
$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}$, and the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $(A,u_{A})$ is the reading of P2
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). No
measurement, no detector, no environment, no external field, no rate and no
record is part of this definition.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are adopted model data and readings. They assert
nothing about a laboratory atom, sample, mode content, cutoff or coupling; no
Maxwell equation, source model, back-reaction or propagation is assumed; the
truncation, the cutoff and the mode vectors are not derived; and no
identification of $\eta_{0}$ or of the $g_{j}$ with laboratory quantities is
made. The identification of a physical preparation with a state of this model
is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The model contains no
photon detector, no sampling model, no environment beyond the declared
transverse modes, and no rate, decay or linewidth statement.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Z^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$; the vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is experimentally determined and $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$. These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: $j$ has dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$; it is a probability flux, not a charge flux.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework, for systems in the declared massive-matter sector, the following statements about states and their composition. Assume throughout the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), which is the choice hypothesis of the mathematical suppliers cited below.

**(i) State space.** To each physical system of the sector the model assigns a complex Hilbert space $H$ that is nonzero and separable: a complex Hilbert space in the sense of [[def-hilbert-space]] which admits a sequence whose range is dense in $H$, so that the hypothesis of [[thm-separable-hilbert-space-has-a-countable-orthonormal-basis]] holds and $H$ has a finite or countable orthonormal basis. The assignment of a Hilbert space to a physical system is a model assumption; the linear structure used to combine descriptions mathematically is not an empirical claim. The physical system to which $H$ is assigned, and the sector in which the assignment is made, are declared with it.

**(ii) Pure preparations.** A **pure preparation** of the system is a unit ray $[\psi]=\{z\psi:z\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}\}$ of a vector $\psi\in H$ with $\|\psi\|=1$; that is, two nonzero vectors describe the same pure preparation exactly when they differ by a nonzero complex factor. The zero vector is not a state and no preparation is assigned to it: the normalization $\|\psi\|=1$ is part of the assignment. The ray allows arbitrary nonzero rescaling; between unit representatives the factor has modulus one and is a **global phase**, which has no observable consequence (P2). The rank-one operator $T_{\psi,\psi}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] is the density operator associated with the ray of $\psi$.

**(iii) General preparations and mixing.** A general preparation of the system is a **density operator**: a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ on $H$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Pure preparations are the special case $\rho=T_{\psi,\psi}$ with $\|\psi\|=1$. A **statistical mixture** of preparations $\rho_{n}$ with weights $w_{n}\ge0$, $\sum_{n}w_{n}=1$, is the trace-norm convergent sum $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ as follows directly in the trace-class Banach space ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]): each density has trace norm one, so $\sum_n\|w_n\rho_n\|_1=1$ gives trace-norm convergence. Every partial sum is positive; operator-norm convergence preserves its nonnegative quadratic forms, and continuity of trace gives $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$ ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]). Thus the limit is again a density operator, without requiring the components to be orthogonal pure states. The weights are a classical preparation uncertainty and are not amplitudes. Distinct weighted ensembles of pure states may define the same $\rho$.

**(iv) Composition.** Two independent distinguishable subsystems with state spaces $H_{A}$ and $H_{B}$ are composed by the completed Hilbert tensor product $H_{A}\widehat\otimes H_{B}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Product preparations $\psi_{A}\otimes\psi_{B}$ are the special case of preparations in which each subsystem has its own specified preparation; general composite preparations are linear combinations and mixtures and need not factor. A quantity of subsystem $A$ alone is represented on the composite by an operator of the form $A\otimes I_{B}$ and a quantity of $B$ alone by $I_{A}\otimes B$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (bounded case; unbounded local operators are treated where they occur). The existence of the completed tensor product is mathematics; the assignment of that product to a composite physical system is the physical assumption here.

**(v) Restrictions that are separate assumptions.** Restrictions of the state space by superselection rules, identical-particle symmetry sectors, and the replacement of the tensor product by more general algebraic structures are not consequences of the clauses above: where such a restriction is used it is adopted separately, and the identical-species sectors are the subject of the postulate P6 of this page.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model within its declared sector. They are not derived from experiment, and they do not assert that a physical system is exactly described by such a Hilbert space; no numerical measurement is recorded. The compatibility of the framework with observation is a question about fully specified models and reported data, in the sense of P7.

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]), let $c$ be a nonzero real and write
$cE := \{\, cx : x \in E \,\}$ for $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$, where
$(cx)_i := cx_i$. Then:

1. $\lambda_n^*(cE) = |c|^{\,n}\,\lambda_n^*(E)$ for every subset $E$, the
   product being defined in $\overline{\mathbb{R}}$ because $|c|^{\,n} > 0$;
2. $E$ is Lebesgue measurable if and only if $cE$ is;
3. $\lambda_n(cE) = |c|^{\,n}\lambda_n(E)$ for every Lebesgue measurable $E$.

At $c = -1$ the map is reflection in the origin and $|c|^{\,n} = 1$, so it
preserves outer measure, measurability and measure. The value $c = 0$ is
excluded because $0E$ is $\{0\}$ or $\varnothing$ and carries no information
about $E$.

before.claim: [Domain and factorisation] Clause (a) is [F1]: each bound state lies in every $D(Q_{i})$, so $D_{q}\psi_{nlm}=-qQ_{q}\psi_{nlm}$ is defined and the matrix element is absolutely convergent. For clause (b), [F1] gives the factorisation $\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},D_{q}\psi_{nlm}\rangle=-q\langle\psi_{n'l'm'},Q_{q}\psi_{nlm}\rangle$ with the displayed radial and angular factors. [F1, algebra]

[Angular vanishing] By [F2] the angular factor in step 1.1 vanishes unless $(l',m')$ is one of the two displayed pairs; because the radial factor is finite, a vanishing angular factor makes the whole matrix element zero. This proves (b). [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

[Necessary conditions] Clause (c) restates step 2.1: $m'-m=q\in\{0,\pm1\}$ and $l'-l\in\{-1,+1\}$ are necessary for a nonvanishing matrix element; the radial factor is not controlled by [F2], so no nonvanishing statement is made for an allowed angular pair, and no probability or rate is defined. [step 2.1, algebra, F2]

[Parity] By [F3], for the harmonic representatives, $\Pi_{\mathrm{par}}\psi_{nlm}=(-1)^{l}\psi_{nlm}$ because the reduced radial function depends on $|x|$ only. 2.1 [Exact averaged comparison] By [F3] at $\delta=\omega_0-\omega=0$ the averaged down-population is $\sin^{2}(|\Omega_{1}|\tau/4)=\sin^{2}(dE_{0}\tau/(2\hbar))$, whose power series begins with $(dE_{0}\tau/(2\hbar))^{2}$, the co-rotating coefficient of step 1.2; the difference between the exact linear-model population and this averaged probability is at most $2\varepsilon(\tau)$ with the displayed $\varepsilon$. [F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Scope] The computation used only the declared two-level data, the prescribed field and the cited driven-dynamics results; no quantized field, vacuum, spontaneous emission, damping or record entered, and the laboratory identifications are P7-tested by [F5]. This is clause (d). [F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **First order versus exact.** The co-rotating component coefficient of clause (b) is the leading term of the exact averaged Rabi oscillation of clause (c) only at small $\tau$; the full linear-drive first-order coefficient is $\gamma_1=|a_++a_-|^2$ and has four times that leading small-time coefficient, so no averaging of the full model is silently assumed; the exact linear model differs from the averaged model by the rotating-wave error, and the exact circular model of the driven-dynamics page is a different declared family, not an approximation proved here.
- **No spontaneous emission.** The example is stimulated: the field is prescribed and unaffected by the transition, and the model contains no vacuum. Spontaneous emission is treated only in the quantized cutoff dipole model of this pair, under the additional vacuum-preparation assumption of the postulate item.

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) for a declared system, in the state, sharp-observable and evolution readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The readings below are the reading of clause (iv) of P4 for the page's models; clause (iv) records that a prescribed time-dependent family is **a different model assumption** from the autonomous one, and clause (b) below adopts it.

**(b) Prescribed energy family.** As an additional model assumption of the pair, fix a nonempty compact interval $I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb R$ of physical times (seconds), the declared state space $\mathfrak H$ of the system, a value $\hbar>0$ of the reduced Planck constant as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and a **prescribed family** $t\mapsto H(t)$ of self-adjoint operators on $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) in one of the following three **regularity classes**, whose hypotheses are part of the model declaration:

- **(i) Bounded norm-continuous class.** $D(H(t))=\mathfrak H$ for every $t$; each $H(t)\in\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is self-adjoint ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); $t\mapsto H(t)$ is norm-continuous on $I$ ([[def-operator-norm]]); and $K:=\sup_{t\in I}\|H(t)\|/\hbar<\infty$.
- **(ii) Bounded-control class.** $H(t)=H_{0}+V(t)$, where $H_{0}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(H_{0})\subseteq\mathfrak H$ and $V:I\to\mathcal B(\mathfrak H)$ is strongly continuous with self-adjoint values and $\|V(t)\|=v(t)$, $v:=\sup_{t\in I}v(t)<\infty$.
- **(iii) Common-domain class.** There is a dense linear subspace $Y\subseteq\mathfrak H$ that is itself a Hilbert space continuously embedded in $\mathfrak H$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], for instance $Y=D(H_{0})$ with the graph norm of a self-adjoint $H_{0}$), with $D(H(t))=Y$ for every $t$, each $H(t)$ self-adjoint as an operator on $\mathfrak H$, and $t\mapsto H(t)$ of class $C^{1}(I;\mathcal B(Y,\mathfrak H))$.

The family, its class and its data are **prescribed**: no field equation, source model, back-reaction or feedback of the system on the source is assumed, and no claim is made that any laboratory arrangement realizes the family. The family is coupled to the system through the material hypotheses of the page or of the item that declares a specific model (for instance a magnetic-moment or electric-dipole coupling, or the external-source Coulomb family of the page's adiabatic models); the reading of $H(t)$ as the energy of the declared system is a model assumption.

**(c) The model's evolution.** The **driven model** declares that the time evolution of the system between times $s,t\in I$ is carried by a family $U(t,s)$ of unitary operators on $\mathfrak H$ with
$$U(s,s)=I,\qquad U(t,r)=U(t,s)U(s,r)\quad(r,s,t\in I),\qquad U(t,s)^{*}=U(s,t),$$
jointly strongly continuous in $(t,s)$, solving the time-dependent Schroedinger equation on $I$ in the sense of the class:
in class (i) $U$ is the unique norm-continuous solution of $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)=H(t)U(t,s)$ with $U(s,s)=I$ constructed by the Dyson series of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-norm-dyson-series-and-uniqueness]] (whose hypothesis is exactly the norm-continuity of the bounded self-adjoint family);
in class (ii) $U$ is the mild propagator constructed in [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-strong-bounded-interaction-picture]], satisfying $U(t,s)\psi=E(t-s)\psi-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int_s^tE(t-r)V(r)U(r,s)\psi\,dr$ for every $\psi\in\mathfrak H$, with $E(u)=e^{-iuH_{0}/\hbar}$ the autonomous flow of clause (b) of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]];
in class (iii) $U$ is the strong propagator of [[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-common-domain-nonautonomous-evolution]] with physical generator $A=H/\hbar$, preserving $Y$, for which $t\mapsto U(t,s)y$ is $C^1$ in $\mathfrak H$ with $i\hbar\partial_tU(t,s)y=H(t)U(t,s)y$ for every $y\in Y$.
In each class the cited item is what makes the declaration well posed: it constructs the family and proves uniqueness under the class hypotheses. The model asserts nothing beyond those hypotheses; in particular it asserts no invariant domain and no strong equation for $H_{0}$-domain vectors in class (ii), and no common domain in classes (i) and (ii).

**(d) State and outcome readings.** The **evolved preparation** at time $t$ of a preparation $\rho$ specified at time $s$ is $\rho(t):=U(t,s)\rho(s)U(t,s)^{*}$; it is a preparation of the model in the sense of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] for every $t$, by unitarity of $U(t,s)$ and [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]. A pure preparation $[\psi(s)]$ evolves to the pure preparation $[\psi(t)]$ with $\psi(t):=U(t,s)\psi(s)\ne0$. The **outcome law at time $t$** of an assigned sharp observable $(A,u_{A})$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]) in that preparation is $\mu^{A}_{\rho(t)}$, the reading of P2; the definition records the timing convention once and asserts nothing about how or when a record is produced.

**(e) Energy-basis amplitudes and level populations.** In class (ii), let $(\varphi_{j})_{j\in J}$ be an orthonormal family in $D(H_{0})$ with $H_{0}\varphi_{j}=E_{j}\varphi_{j}$ and $E_{j}\in\mathbb R$ (a complete orthonormal family of eigenvectors is not assumed here). For $s\le t$ and labels $i,j$ the **transition amplitude from $i$ at time $s$ to $j$ at time $t$** is the scalar
$$A_{ji}(t,s):=e^{iE_{j}(t-s)/\hbar}\,\bigl\langle U(t,s)\varphi_{i},\varphi_{j}\bigr\rangle ,$$
and the **transition probability** is $p_{ji}(t,s):=|A_{ji}(t,s)|^{2}$. If additionally $E_{j}$ is a simple eigenvalue of $H_{0}$ with spectral projection $P_{j}=E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})$ onto $\mathbb C\varphi_{j}$, then the definition *states*, as the reading of P2, the identity
$$p_{ji}(t,s)=\mu^{H_{0}}_{\psi(t)}(\{E_{j}\})=\|E_{H_{0}}(\{E_{j}\})\psi(t)\|^{2},\qquad \psi(t)=U(t,s)\varphi_{i},$$
which follows from the rank-one form of $P_{j}$ and the normalization $\|\varphi_{j}\|=1$; $p_{ji}$ is the reading of the outcome probability of the value $E_{j}$ of the assigned energy observable $(H_{0},\mathrm J)$ in the evolved preparation, and it is a property of the declared model, not a measured frequency.

**(f) Declared two-level drive models.** Let $(\sigma_{x},\sigma_{y},\sigma_{z})$ be the Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] clause (e) acting on $\mathbb C^{2}$ in the orthonormal basis $(e_{\uparrow},e_{\downarrow})$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), let $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega\in\mathbb R$, and put $H_{0}:=\frac{\hbar}{2}\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}$ (class (i) with $I$ any compact interval). The **circular two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm c}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\bigl(\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}+\sin(\omega t)\sigma_{y}\bigr)\Bigr),$$
and the **linear two-level drive model** is the class-(i) family
$$H_{\mathrm l}(t):=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\omega_{0}\sigma_{z}+\Omega_{1}\cos(\omega t)\sigma_{x}\bigr).$$
The dimensionless numbers $\omega_{0},\Omega_{1},\omega$ are read as angular frequencies in $\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; $\omega_{0}$ is the **splitting frequency** of the model (the level gap is $\hbar|\omega_{0}|$), $\omega$ the **drive frequency**, $\Omega_{1}$ the **transverse coupling**, and $\Delta:=\omega_{0}-\omega$ the **detuning**. Populations of the level pair are the diagonal entries $\langle P_{\bullet}\psi,\psi\rangle$ of the orthogonal projections $P_{\uparrow},P_{\downarrow}$ onto $\mathbb Ce_{\uparrow},\mathbb Ce_{\downarrow}$ in the evolved vector $\psi(t)$. The two families are model data: no identification with a laboratory spin, molecule or field, and no relation of $\Omega_{1}$ to a field amplitude, is asserted; such an identification is a tested identification in the sense of P7.

**(g) Status and scope.** Clauses (b), (c), (f) are adopted model assumptions and readings; the existence and uniqueness of the propagator in each class is cited mathematics, not a consequence of P1, P2 or P4. The model asserts no open-system or environment coupling, no non-unitary reduced dynamics, no measurement or apparatus model, no thermalization or equilibration, no long-time limit and no empirical record; the identification of the family's parameters with laboratory fields and of the system with a laboratory sample is made, if at all, only in separately declared models with their own uncertainty.

Let $s\in\frac12\mathbb N=\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$, put $N:=2s\in\mathbb N$ and let
$V_s:=\mathbb C^{N+1}$ carry the standard inner product
$\langle z,w\rangle=\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k\overline{w_k}$, linear in the first argument
([[def-inner-product-space]]). Write $(e_m)_{-s\le m\le s}$ for the standard basis, indexed so that
$e_m$ is the vector with entry $1$ in position $k=s-m$ and entry $0$ elsewhere; thus
$\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=1$ if $m=n$ and $\langle e_m,e_n\rangle=0$ otherwise. Define $\mathbb C$-linear maps
$J_z,J_+,J_-\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V_s)$ by their values on this basis ([[def-linear-map]]):

$$J_ze_m:=m\,e_m,\qquad J_+e_m:=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}\,e_{m+1},\qquad J_-e_m:=\sqrt{(s+m)(s-m+1)}\,e_{m-1},$$

where $e_{s+1}:=0$ and $e_{-s-1}:=0$, and put

$$J_x:=\tfrac12(J_++J_-),\qquad J_y:=\tfrac1{2i}(J_+-J_-),\qquad J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2 .$$

Then:

(a) $J_z$, $J_x$ and $J_y$ are self-adjoint endomorphisms of $V_s$
([[def-self-adjoint-and-normal-endomorphism]]), and $J_+^*=J_-$, $J_-^*=J_+$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]]);

(b) on $V_s$ the commutators are

$$[J_z,J_+]=J_+,\qquad [J_z,J_-]=-J_-,\qquad [J_+,J_-]=2J_z,\qquad [J_x,J_y]=iJ_z,\qquad [J_y,J_z]=iJ_x,\qquad [J_z,J_x]=iJ_y ;$$

(c) $J^2=J_-J_++J_z^2+J_z=J_+J_-+J_z^2-J_z=s(s+1)I$, and $[J^2,J_z]=[J^2,J_\pm]=0$;

(d) the matrix elements of the raising operator are
$\|J_+e_m\|^2=(s-m)(s+m+1)$ and $\|J_-e_m\|^2=(s+m)(s-m+1)$, and
$\langle J_+e_m,e_{m+1}\rangle=\sqrt{(s-m)(s+m+1)}$, which is nonzero exactly when $m<s$;

(e) for $s=\tfrac12$, identify $V_{\frac12}=\mathbb C^2$ with the basis ordered as $(e_{\frac12},e_{-\frac12})$ and let

$$\sigma_x:=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_y:=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\ i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_z:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

be the Pauli matrices. Then $J_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ for $i=x,y,z$, $\sigma_x^2=\sigma_y^2=\sigma_z^2=I$,
$\sigma_x\sigma_y=i\sigma_z$, $\sigma_y\sigma_z=i\sigma_x$, $\sigma_z\sigma_x=i\sigma_y$, and consequently
$\sigma_i\sigma_j+\sigma_j\sigma_i=2\delta_{ij}I$ and $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\delta_{ij}I+i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}\sigma_k$ for all $i,j$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise, and $\varepsilon_{ijk}$ denotes the sign of the permutation $(x,y,z)\mapsto(i,j,k)$.

All statements are finite-dimensional linear algebra: no physical interpretation of $J_x,J_y,J_z$ as angular momentum, and no measurement postulate, is asserted here.

Adopt the prescribed dipole-drive model of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]] with its
matter data $W\simeq\mathbb C^{d}$, $H_{a}$, $D^{W}_{1},D^{W}_{2},D^{W}_{3}$ and
its compact interval $I=[t_{0},t_{1}]$, the driven model of
[[def-nrqm-driven-dynamics-framework-driven-model]] clause (b)(i) and the
framework readings of P1, P2 and P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axioms of
Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $v_{i},v_{k}$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of
$H_{a}$ with $H_{a}v_{i}=E_{i}v_{i}$, $H_{a}v_{k}=E_{k}v_{k}$, put
$\Delta:=E_{k}-E_{i}$, $\tau:=t-s$ and let
$A_{ki}(t,s)=e^{i\Delta\tau/\hbar}\langle U(t,s)v_{i},v_{k}\rangle$ be the
model's transition amplitude of clause (e) of the driven model with
$U(t,s)$ the propagator of the drive family
$H_{\mathrm d}(r)=H_{a}-\sum_{j}E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)D^{W}_{j}$. Then:

(a) (first-order amplitude and remainder) with
$$A^{(1)}_{ki}(t,s)=\frac{i}{\hbar}\sum_{j=1}^{3}\int_{s}^{t} e^{i\Delta(r-s)/\hbar}\,E_{\mathrm{ext},j}(r)\, \bigl\langle D^{W}_{j}v_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\,dr,$$
one has $A_{ki}(t,s)=\delta_{ik}+A^{(1)}_{ki}(t,s)+R_{ki}(t,s)$ with
$|R_{ki}(t,s)|\le e^{K\tau}(K\tau)^{2}/2$, where
$K:=\sup_{r\in I}\|H_{\mathrm d}(r)\|/\hbar$; in particular the first-order
amplitude is the model's exact amplitude up to the displayed Dyson remainder;

(b) (monochromatic co- and counter-rotating terms) if
$\mathbf E_{\mathrm{ext}}(r)=\mathbf E_{0}\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ with
$\mathbf E_{0}\in\mathbb R^{3}$, $\omega,\vartheta\in\mathbb R$ and
$W:=-\sum_{j}E_{0,j}D^{W}_{j}$ (a bounded self-adjoint operator on $W$), then
$V(r)=W\cos(\omega r+\vartheta)$ and
$$A^{(1)}_{ki}=a_{+}+a_{-},\qquad a_{\pm}=-\frac{i}{2\hbar}\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle e^{\mp i\vartheta_{0}}\frac{e^{i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)\tau/\hbar}-1} {i(\Delta\mp\hbar\omega)/\hbar},\qquad \vartheta_{0}:=\omega s+\vartheta,$$
with the value $\tau$ for the quotient when $\Delta\mp\hbar\omega=0$;
consequently the co-rotating term satisfies
$$|a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\, \frac{\bigl|\sin\bigl((\Delta-\hbar\omega)\tau/(2\hbar)\bigr)\bigr|} {|\Delta-\hbar\omega|} \quad(\Delta\ne\hbar\omega),\qquad |a_{+}|=\bigl|\bigl\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\bigr\rangle\bigr|\frac{\tau}{2\hbar} \quad(\Delta=\hbar\omega),$$
and the counter-rotating term satisfies
$|a_{-}|\le|\langle Wv_{i},v_{k}\rangle|/|\Delta+\hbar\omega|$ whenever
$\Delta+\hbar\omega\ne0$;

(c) (equal stimulated coefficients) for the two-level case $d=2$ with
orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{\uparrow},v_{\downarrow}$, $H_{a}v_{\uparrow}
=E_{\uparrow}v_{\uparrow}$, $H_{a}v_{\downarrow}=E_{\downarrow}v_{\downarrow}$
and $\Delta=E_{\uparrow}-E_{\downarrow}>0$, the first-order amplitudes for the
upward transition $\downarrow\to\uparrow$ and the downward transition
